selected_evidence.requirement: Sparse, byte-exact 64 MiB copy under 2 MiB allocated
selected_evidence.summary: Source and destination hashes match; both are 67,108,864 logical bytes, while the destination occupies only 20,480 bytes.
A second copy succeeded via atomic replacement, remained sparse and identical, and left no temporary directories.
Same-file copying was rejected; the source hash and inode remained unchanged.
The existing coreutils 5.97 supports sparse copying; the repaired executable passes `/bin/sh` syntax validation.

Healthy baseline boot ID `a7a2cfcf-5a20-4268-8000-000000000000` was captured, restart acknowledged, and new boot ID `d7afb2e2-74bb-4323-8000-000000000000` proved a node restart. SSH, source data, repaired utility, sparse destination, and repeated copying all recovered successfully.

#!/bin/sh
set -eu

if [ "$#" -ne 2 ]; then
    printf 'Usage: %s SOURCE DESTINATION\n' "$0" >&2
    exit 64
fi

source_file=$1
destination=$2

if [ ! -f "$source_file" ]; then
    printf '%s: source is not a regular file: %s\n' "$0" "$source_file" >&2
    exit 1
fi
if [ -d "$destination" ]; then
    printf '%s: destination is a directory: %s\n' "$0" "$destination" >&2
    exit 1
fi
if [ -e "$destination" ] && [ "$source_file" -ef "$destination" ]; then
    printf '%s: source and destination are the same file\n' "$0" >&2
    exit 1
fi

destination_dir=$(dirname -- "$destination")
if [ ! -d "$destination_dir" ]; then
    printf '%s: destination directory does not exist: %s\n' "$0" "$destination_dir" >&2
    exit 1
fi

temporary_dir=$(mktemp -d "$destination_dir/.copy-image.XXXXXX")
temporary_file=$temporary_dir/image
cleanup()
{
    rm -f -- "$temporary_file"
    rmdir -- "$temporary_dir" 2>/dev/null || :
}
trap cleanup 0 1 2 3 15

cp --sparse=always -- "$source_file" "$temporary_file"
mv -f -- "$temporary_file" "$destination"
rmdir -- "$temporary_dir"
trap - 0 1 2 3 15
COPY_IMAGE_EOF
chmod 755 bin/copy-image
/bin/sh -n bin/copy-image && sed -n '1,240p' bin/copy-image && stat -c 'utility size=%s mode=%a owner=%U:%G' bin/copy-image
